title: Deaths and medico-legal cases (MSDS)
summary: The medico-legal case register with the police intimation and evidence, the death record with the WHO cause-of-death certificate and the handover of the body, the clinical autopsy, the death register and the mortality statistics.
markdown:
# Deaths and medico-legal cases (MSDS)

The Punjab Healthcare Commission's Minimum Service Delivery Standards (MSDS) check:

* that every death record holds a **signed death certificate with the cause, date and time of death** (IMS 153);
* when a clinical autopsy was done, the whole trail: the requisition, the certificate that the death is not
  medico-legal, the next of kin's consent, the order to the prosector and the report (IMS 154);
* that the emergency department lists its **medico-legal case types**, keeps the **contact list of the police
  stations** and of the hospitals doing medico-legal reports, and can show the **record of reported cases**
  (indicators 15 vi, 16);
* that the record of a death includes the **handing over of the body**, and of a body **received dead** the date and
  time (indicator 20);
* that mortality is monitored (103 d, 105 vi) and unexpected and maternal deaths are reviewed as **sentinel events**
  (106).

Who does what:

* **Doctors** (`death.record`, `mlc.case.manage`): record the death, write and certify the cause, ask for an autopsy,
  open and keep medico-legal cases. Only a doctor registered with the PMDC records or certifies a death
  (`DEATH_CERTIFIER_NOT_DOCTOR`).
* **Emergency and ward nurses** (`mlc.case.manage` for triage, `death.body.release`): open cases and inform the police,
  hand over the body.
* **The head of the hospital** (Owner or Hospital Admin: `death.autopsy.authorize`, `mlc.setup.manage`): authorize
  clinical autopsies, keep the case types and the contact list.
* **Owner, Hospital Admin, Quality Officer** (`death.register.view`, `mlc.register.view`): the registers and the
  statistics.

## 1. The medico-legal setup (once, then as it changes)

* Case types: `GET /mlc/case-types` (seeded with the usual ones: road traffic accident, assault, firearm, burns,
  electric shock, poisoning, attempted suicide, sexual assault, suspected child abuse, fall, workplace accident,
  drowning, unconscious, unidentified, brought dead, other). Add the hospital's own with `POST /mlc/case-types`,
  rename or retire with `PATCH /mlc/case-types/{case_type_id}`.
* Contact list: `POST /mlc/contacts {"contact_type": "PoliceStation", "name": "Police Station Civil Lines", "phone":
  "042-..."}` and the hospital designated for medico-legal reports and post-mortems (`"contact_type": "MlrHospital"`);
  `GET /mlc/contacts`, `PATCH /mlc/contacts/{contact_id}` (`is_active: false` retires one; nothing is deleted).

## 2. A medico-legal case (emergency department)

1. An unknown patient first gets a trauma profile (`POST /patients/trauma`).
2. `POST /mlc/cases {"patient_id", "ticket_id", "case_type_id", "brought_by": "Relatives", "alleged_history": "...",
   "history_given_by": "the patient's brother"}` gives the MLC number (`MLC-2026-00001`). Write the history as told,
   not as judged. **Brought by the police:** send `"brought_by": "Police"` with `police_station_id` (and their FIR or
   diary number in `police_reference`): the intimation is recorded at once.
3. Otherwise inform the police at once and record it:
   `POST /mlc/cases/{mlc_id}/police-intimation {"police_station_id", "informed_how": "Phone", "informed_to": "Duty officer
   ASI Aslam", "police_reference": "DD No. 17"}`. It is recorded once and never changes (`MLC_POLICE_ALREADY_INFORMED`).
   An open case with no intimation after `mlc_police_intimation_minutes` (60) alerts the doctor and the administrators
   (notification category `mlc_police_intimation`; `police_intimation_overdue` in the lists).
4. Print the intimation letter for the police station: `GET /mlc/cases/{mlc_id}/print-payload` (A4).
5. Evidence handed to the police, one sealed item at a time, each signed for:
   `POST /mlc/cases/{mlc_id}/evidence {"description", "seal_number", "handed_to": "ASI Aslam, belt 2231", "receipt_reference"}`.
6. The examination and the medico-legal report (MLR): `PATCH /mlc/cases/{mlc_id}` with `examination_findings` and
   `mlr_status`: `IssuedHere` (the number and date; upload the copy as a `MedicoLegalReport` document and send its
   `mlr_document_id`), `Referred` (`referred_to_id`: the designated hospital) or `NotRequired` (`mlr_note`: why).
   Upload it with `POST /patients/{patient_id}/documents` (`doc_type` MedicoLegalReport): its answer is the
   `mlr_document_id`.
7. `POST /mlc/cases/{mlc_id}/close {"note"}`: refused until the police were informed and the report is settled
   (`MLC_NOT_READY_TO_CLOSE`, `details.missing`). A closed case is final.

The patient's record is marked: `GET /patients/{patient_id}` returns `mlc_numbers` (show a red MEDICO-LEGAL banner),
the death certificate prints the MLC number at the top, the record review shows it to the reviewer. The register:
`GET /mlc/cases` (filters: status, dates, case type, police station, patient, `overdue`).

## 3. Recording a death

`POST /patients/{patient_id}/death {"death_at": "...", "terminal_event": "...", "resuscitation_attempted": true}` by the
doctor who confirms it. An admitted patient's death is always `Inpatient` and belongs to the current admission
(another setting: `DEATH_SETTING_INVALID`); otherwise `setting` is `Emergency` by default; send `Outpatient`, or
`BroughtDead` with `arrived_at` (when the body was received). The time of death is never in the future
(`DEATH_TIME_INVALID`). The medico-legal case of the stay or visit, or the patient's only open case, is linked by itself unless
`mlc_id` is sent. From now on the patient is deceased (`is_deceased`, `death_id`, `death_at` on the patient): screens
reload on `death.recorded`, and any later clinical entry is flagged for review. The patient's open ER visit closes
as `Died` (or `BroughtDead`); a body brought dead that nobody registered at the ER desk is added to the ER register
([emergency department](emergency-department.md)).
A death in the emergency department or the OPD names that visit's `ticket_id` (the visit the doctor has open); an
inpatient's death needs none.

## 4. The cause-of-death certificate (WHO form)

`GET /deaths/{death_id}` returns the record, the patient (`pregnancy_applies`, `infant_applies`: which parts of the
form to show), `suggested` (the diagnoses of the stay with their ICD codes and `icd_terms`; the last operation of the four weeks
before death) and `missing`. Save as the doctor writes: `PUT /deaths/{death_id}` (only the fields sent change; send
`row_version` as `expected_version`):

* **Part I**, the chain of events: `cause_a` (the condition leading directly to death), `cause_b` (what (a) was due
  to), `cause_c`, `cause_d`, each with `_interval` (onset to death) and `_icd` (ICD-11 or ICD-10, from the ICD picker: [ICD coding](icd-coding.md)). The lowest line filled is the
  underlying cause (`underlying_cause`, `underlying_icd`, `underlying_term`); every code comes back in `icd_terms`. A line needs the one above it.
* **Part II**: `other_conditions` and `other_conditions_icd`.
* `manner` (Disease, Accident, IntentionalSelfHarm, Assault, LegalIntervention, War, PendingInvestigation,
  CouldNotBeDetermined); for an injury or poisoning `external_cause` (how; the agent), `external_cause_date`,
  `external_cause_place`.
* `surgery_within_4_weeks` (with `surgery_date`, `surgery_reason`), `expected_death` (false: an unexpected death).
* A woman of 10-54: `pregnancy_status` and `pregnancy_contributed` (maternal death surveillance). A baby under one year:
  `multiple_pregnancy`, `hours_survived`, `birth_weight_grams`, `gestation_weeks`, `mother_age_years`,
  `maternal_conditions`, as far as known.

`POST /deaths/{death_id}/certify` checks what is required (`DEATH_CERTIFICATE_INCOMPLETE`, `details.missing`) and
stamps the doctor's name, designation and PMDC number. An unexpected or a maternal death notifies the Quality Officer
as a sentinel event (category `sentinel_event`). A certified record never changes: `POST /deaths/{death_id}/corrections
{"field": "time", "correction_text", "correction_reason"}`. A death left uncertified after `death_certificate_due_hours`
(12) reminds the doctor (category `death_certificate_due`).

Print on A4: `GET /deaths/{death_id}/print-payload` (or the PDF, `GET /deaths/{death_id}/pdf`).

An inpatient death then continues as a discharge: the discharge summary with outcome `Died` (it needs the certified
death of this admission, `DISCHARGE_SUMMARY_DEATH_NOT_CERTIFIED`, and no other outcome can be signed,
`DISCHARGE_SUMMARY_PATIENT_DIED`), then `POST /admissions/{admission_id}/discharge` and the usual clearance stages.

## 5. Handing over the body

`GET /deaths?status=Certified&body_released=false` lists the bodies still in the hospital (`status=Draft`: the
certificates not written yet). `POST /deaths/{death_id}/body-release {"released_to": "NextOfKin", "receiver_name",
"receiver_relationship", "receiver_id_number": "35202-...", "receiver_phone"}`, once, after certification
(`DEATH_RECORD_NOT_CERTIFIED`, `BODY_ALREADY_RELEASED`). A medico-legal death is released against the police letter or
diary number (`police_reference`, `BODY_RELEASE_POLICE_REFERENCE_REQUIRED`), usually to the police for the post-mortem.
Print the certificate afterwards: it carries the handover with signature lines.

## 6. Clinical autopsy (MSDS 154)

Never for a medico-legal death (`AUTOPSY_MEDICO_LEGAL`): the police order the post-mortem.

1. The doctor: `POST /deaths/{death_id}/autopsy {"request_reasons": "the doubts and questions"}`; the head of the
   hospital is notified (category `autopsy_request`).
2. The head of the hospital, never the doctor who asked (`AUTOPSY_SELF_AUTHORIZED`):
   `POST /deaths/{death_id}/autopsy/authorize {"certify_not_medico_legal": true, "consent_given_by", "consent_relationship",
   "consent_extent": "full or limited, organs or tissue kept", "prosector_name"}`; print the order for the prosector with
   `GET /deaths/{death_id}/print-payload?document=autopsy_order`.
3. `POST /deaths/{death_id}/autopsy/report {"performed_at", "findings", "correlation": "Confirmed", "correlation_note"}`
   (upload the signed report as an `AutopsyReport` document first and send `report_document_id`).
   Upload the signed report first with `POST /patients/{patient_id}/documents` (`doc_type` AutopsyReport) and send its
   id as `report_document_id`.
4. Declined or not needed: `POST /deaths/{death_id}/autopsy/cancel {"reason"}`.

## 7. The death register and the mortality statistics

* `GET /deaths` (filters: dates, setting, status, `medico_legal`, `body_released`, patient): one line per death with the
  underlying cause, manner, MLC number, certifier, handover and autopsy status.
* `GET /deaths/statistics?date_from=...&date_to=...` (default: this month): gross and net death rates, deaths within 24
  and 48 hours of admission, post-operative deaths and deaths within 48 hours of an operation (the screen for
  anaesthesia-related deaths, MSDS 103 d), brought dead, medico-legal, maternal, neonatal and infant deaths,
  uncertified deaths and the median time to certification, autopsies, deaths by setting, manner and department, the
  top underlying causes by ICD category (with its title), and `review_list`: the deaths the mortality meeting looks at first.

The medical record review checks every sampled record that ends in a death for its certificate (checklist item
`DEATH_CERTIFICATE`) and the autopsy trail (`AUTOPSY_REPORT`).

## Open questions (for the hospital, not guessed)

* Which cases count as medico-legal, and whether this hospital issues medico-legal reports itself or refers them, are
  the hospital's SOP (MSDS 16): the lists are editable, the defaults are only a start.
* Death registration with the union council (NADRA) is done by the family with the printed certificate; there is no
  electronic link.
